Replay

Durable Room checkpoints

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
State and lifetimeShared control I/OIntegration and bounds

room_save(&room) starts an asynchronous publication of a live host's state to the configured checkpoint service. room_frame owns status lookup, snapshot capture, transfer and completion while gameplay, authority renewals and ordinary successor replication continue.

Odin
// Optional automatic publication; zero keeps saves manual.
options.checkpoint_interval_ms = 10000
// The default requires verified WSS. Explicit local development may use loopback WS.
options.checkpoint_local_development = local_development

// After room_open, call room_frame normally. A menu can also request a save:
error := replaygd.room_save(&room)
// None means requested. A durable receipt arrives asynchronously:
if room.save.phase == .Saved {
    saved_tick := room.save.publication.point.archive.tick
}

The service must support the deployment's content/model and dependency policy. checkpoint_assets declares/validates external dependencies and checkpoint_cache supplies their bytes. Room publishes a complete package when dependencies are present; missing bytes prevent publication. Plain remote WebSocket and ENet control are refused for publication; verified WSS is supported, with an explicit loopback WS development opt-in. Party_Config.checkpoint_interval_ms passes the interval into its Room options and retains Party's existing local development choice. Valid automatic intervals are 1–120 seconds.

State and lifetime#

  • Checking reads the latest durable publication revision. A signed Missing response permits the first publication. Other status failures do not capture or upload a new checkpoint.
  • Uploading owns a complete immutable prepared checkpoint. Room captures the current world after status completes, derives the next archive sequence in the current epoch, and publishes against the observed revision. At most one operation is active. A second manual request returns Busy.
  • Saved names a durable, authenticated publication. completed counts successful receipts, including recovery of an exact earlier committed attempt.
  • Interrupted means authority/connection/registration changed or the control connection was explicitly paused. Failed includes service errors and timeouts. An interrupted/failed upload may already have committed: uncertain records that ambiguity. Neither state asserts that the previous durable save was lost.

The owned prepared bytes survive an interrupted upload until the next attempt or Room close. A retry first reads current status. If the exact publisher/Point is already stored, Room acknowledges it without publishing again. Otherwise it records the latest authenticated publication and captures current state for a new attempt. This does not claim that an older, now-superseded request never committed.

publication always describes the latest durable metadata observed; it may be from a previous host. attempts, serial, last_started, error and uncertain expose progress. Metadata and operation counters survive control reconnects within the Room lifetime. Closing Room releases the checkpoint client and prepared bytes.

Only a registered live host may start or continue publication. Followers, handoff and fenced phases cannot capture a new save. A role/epoch/coordinator-generation change closes the old transfer. The service still independently enforces current identity/nonce/connection binding, hosting permissions, live lease, typed model validation, full Record/publication CAS and final commit authorization.

Automatic saving starts when the Room first becomes eligible, then keeps at least the configured interval between starts. It never overlaps operations or blocks play waiting for a result. Persistent save errors remain observable and subsequent automatic attempts follow the same interval.

Shared control I/O#

After status resolves, Room obtains a fresh successful authority renewal before capturing/packaging a new checkpoint. The expensive work therefore starts with a refreshed lease rather than the remainder of the status round trip. Existing lease duration and fencing rules remain unchanged.

Room now has one bounded control receiver that dispatches checkpoint and authority RPC packets before pumping outgoing RPC work. The borrowed RPC transport copy has reads/polling temporarily disabled during that outgoing pump, then restored. It cannot drain checkpoint traffic accidentally. Existing control pause behavior is preserved; checkpoint work stops while ordinary lease expiry remains in force.

room_control_pump and room_save_frame are lower-level driver steps used by room_frame and transport-independent lifecycle tests. Normal games should call room_frame once; they should not additionally drive these steps or drain the control transport independently.

Integration and bounds#

Cavecrawl's online host can use its existing save action/F5 or the party checkpoint button. REPLAY_CAVE_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MS opts into automatic publication (zero by default); browser launch parameters use room_checkpoint_ms. Solo/local save slots remain separate. The native party test verifies both the original host's publication and the successor's newer-epoch publication, then decodes the actual stored inventory.

The browser party gate also exercises both publications through Room during real RTC play, alongside a second isolated room, migration and durable rejoin. It uses explicit loopback development WS. A fresh native reader validates the saved successor inventory; this is not production browser TLS/deployment evidence.

These operations save simulation checkpoints and their declared packaged asset bytes. Personal profiles remain separate. Publication does not supply a restore grant or guarantee preservation after the reported saved tick. Room now separately drives fresh-process party restoration, with native/browser Cavecrawl acceptance. Broader asset profiles and other game acceptance remain part of M5. See the service contract and checkpoint transport.
